guideTitle: Best 70 Pint Dehumidifiers with Drain Hoses (2026)
metaDescription: Six 70 pint class dehumidifiers with drain hoses compared on gravity drainage, tank backup, auto shutoff, noise and defrost for damp lower levels.
expertTake: The Ludatido 2026 is the pick for most buyers: Energy Star, a 35 dB claim and a 1.32 gallon backup tank. The AIRPLUS continuous-drain model is the value pick for a simple gravity setup. Skip a hose-only unit if your drain sits above the machine, because gravity will not move the water uphill.
introParagraphs: A drain hose is the cheapest upgrade a big dehumidifier can have. It removes the daily chore of carrying a heavy tank, keeps the machine running while you are away, and avoids the overflow that happens when a full bucket cuts the unit off in the middle of the night.

A hose works by gravity, though, so everything depends on where the machine sits relative to the drain. The details that matter are the fitting, the backup tank, how the shutoff behaves, and whether the machine can handle a cool room.

products.name: Ludatido 2026 80 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier with Hose
products.description:
The 2026 Ludatido pairs Energy Star certification with a stated 35 dB working noise from an upgraded compressor and fan structure. That is among the quietest claims in the class and makes sense for a finished basement. It also covers 5,000 square feet by the claim and ships with a hose for continuous drainage.

The 1.32 gallon tank is the backup route when the hose is disconnected or the drain clogs. A hose with a backup tank is the safest setup, because a full tank stops the machine, while a hose alone can fail silently. Compared with the older Ludatido model, this one adds the Energy Star label and the lower noise claim, and sits in the lowest price tier here.

Slope the hose downhill, check the fitting after the first week and clean the filter monthly. Since the working rating is not printed, treat the 80 pint figure as a ceiling and watch the first week of output. In year three, the fan and float are the parts to check, and both are easy to reach. If you plan to hide the hose behind a finished wall or a stud bay, test the run first with the wall open, because a hidden leak is the hardest kind to find. Pair it with a hygrometer so you can confirm the quiet claim does not come at the cost of output.
products.bestFor: Finished basements that want a quiet hose-drained machine at a low price tier.
pros: Lowest price tier in the lineup
cons: Newer brand with limited service reach

products.name: AIRPLUS 70 Pint Dehumidifier with Continuous Drain Hose
products.description:
This AIRPLUS states its test condition: 70 pints at 86F and 90 percent humidity. That is cooler than the usual 95F peak and gives a more believable number. The listing stresses the labor saving of a continuous hose compared with manual drainage.

It is a plain compressor machine with no pump, so the drain must sit below it. It sits in a low price tier and states that performance varies with temperature, humidity and airflow. Against the Ludatido, it gives up the Energy Star label and the noise figure, but it is cheaper and simpler.

Use it where a floor drain is within a few feet of the machine. Wash the filter monthly and clean the tank when you check the hose. Because it relies on gravity alone, set it on a low platform beside the drain and test the hose with a bucket of water before leaving it. A kinked line is the usual cause of an overflow. The bedroom positioning is a hint that this model is meant to be heard as little as possible, though it does not publish a decibel figure.
products.bestFor: Simple gravity-drained setups with a floor drain beside the machine.
pros: Notes that performance varies with conditions

products.name: Moiswell 70 Pint Commercial Dehumidifier with Gravity Drain
products.description:
Moiswell sells the Defender ME-7 as a commercial, Energy Star certified machine with a gravity drainage system. Gravity is the simple, reliable method: water leaves through a hose by falling, so there is no motor to fail. The large display panel makes settings easy to read.

Commercial builds tolerate dust and cold, so it fits a crawl space, a garage or an unfinished basement. It is louder than a residential unit and sits in a high price tier. The listing does not publish a working rating, so treat 70 pints as a peak.

Plan the drain first: the outlet must be higher than the hose end. Clean the filter on schedule. Because gravity is the only route, a crawl space with no low drain is a poor fit, so confirm the layout before buying. A short hose run to a floor drain or a sump is ideal. Place it on a firm shelf or block, away from direct splash, and give it clearance so the large display stays readable.
products.bestFor: Crawl spaces and utility areas with a low drain.
pros: Gravity drain has no pump to fail

products.name: Kesnos 80 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier 6,000 sq ft
products.description:
Kesnos offers two drainage options with auto shutoff and a 1.06 gallon tank, plus a 30 to 80 percent humidity range. The shutoff matters because a hose that disconnects or clogs will otherwise let the tank overflow. It carries Energy Star certification.

The 6,000 square foot claim is the largest here, but treat it as an upper bound. It sits in a lower-middle price tier. Compared with the Ludatido, it lacks a noise claim and has a smaller backup tank.

Slope the hose, test the shutoff once, and clean the filter monthly. Test the auto shutoff once by lifting the tank slightly, so you know it works before you rely on it. The large coverage claim is a reminder to size by the room, not by the label. The wide 30 to 80 percent range lets you hold a very dry level for stored items or ease off for living space.
products.bestFor: Large open spaces where a big coverage claim and Energy Star matter.
pros: Largest coverage claim at 6,000 sq ft

products.name: Yaufey 80 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier 5,500 sq ft
products.description:
Yaufey states its 95F and 90 percent test, so you know the 80 pint figure is a hot peak. The unit carries Energy Star certification, a 5,500 square foot claim and a tank with automatic shutoff. A continuous drain hose is the intended route.

It is a mid-low price tier machine with no noise figure. Compared with the Kesnos, it states its test while the Kesnos does not, but it gives up a little coverage.

Check the hose fitting after the first week and keep the line sloped. Keep a foot of clearance behind the exhaust and keep stored boxes away from the intake so airflow stays strong. Verify the hose fitting is snug after the first day. Over a long season the Energy Star label matters more than the peak number, since the machine will run for months.
products.bestFor: Basements with a nearby floor drain and a buyer who values a stated test.

products.name: Prikod 70 Pint Commercial Dehumidifier with Pump and Hose
products.description:
Prikod combines a pump and a drain hose, so you can run it by gravity or lift. It lists auto defrost and auto restart, with operation in cold garages and basements as low as 41F. That cold limit is among the lowest in this guide.

The 70 pint rate is described as based on hot, humid summer conditions, so expect less in a cool room. It is an Energy Star commercial machine with a washable filter. It sits in a high price tier.

Flush the pump line each season and check the hose. In a cold cellar, let the unit run through the first defrost cycle before judging output, and slope the hose so it does not hold standing water that could freeze. The washable filter is a small plus, because a crawl space or garage fills the filter quickly with dust.
products.bestFor: Cold garages and cellars where the drain may be high or low.
pros: Pump and hose give flexible routing
cons: 70 pint figure is a summer peak

buyingCriteria.explanation: A hose works only if the outlet sits below the machine. Raise the unit on a block and slope the line with no loops. If the drain is above the floor, a pump unit like the Prikod is the answer. As a rule, add one foot of slope per ten feet of hose, because a flat line holds water and slows flow until it overflows.

A hose can disconnect or clog. A tank with auto shutoff, as on the Kesnos and Yaufey, prevents an overflow. The Ludatido's 1.32 gallon tank is the largest backup here. Always choose a model that can fall back on its tank, because a clogged hose is the most common cause of a flooded floor.

AIRPLUS states 70 pints at 86F and 90 percent. Yaufey states 95F and 90 percent. The 2019 US test is 65F and 60 percent, so working output is lower. If you rely on a stated test, compare the temperature first, because a number measured at 86F is closer to a basement than one at 95F.

A hose line can freeze in a cold garage. Prikod lists operation down to 41F and auto defrost. A standard unit loses output below about 65F. A hose line in an unheated space can freeze, so choose a cold-rated unit or insulate the line.

Ludatido claims 35 dB. Commercial units like the Moiswell are louder. For a finished space, check the low-speed figure. For a finished space, look for the lowest published speed rather than the average figure.

A 70 pint class machine draws roughly 600 to 900 watts. Energy Star on five of the six picks lowers running cost. Check the Energy Star listing for the exact model, since brands sometimes share names across units. A short test with a bucket of water tells you more about a hose setup than any listing.

cards.label: Gravity
cards.text: AIRPLUS, Ludatido, Kesnos, Yaufey and Moiswell need a low drain but have no pump to fail.

cards.label: Pump
cards.text: Prikod can lift water and still has a hose.

howToChoose.note: Choose gravity if the drain is low.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A quiet low speed, a backup tank and a hose that stays out of sight.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The drain is high or the room is cold. The Prikod and Moiswell earn it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The drain is low and the room is mild. The AIRPLUS covers it.

maintenance.why: A loose fitting leaks. Do it after any long shutdown.
A blocked filter frosts the coil. Dry it fully before refilling.
Algae slows flow. Replace the hose if it stiffens.
Dust blocks heat transfer. Use a soft brush and unplug first.
Sensors drift about 5 percent. Compare with a separate meter.

faq.q: How long should the hose be?
faq.a: Measure from the outlet to the drain and add a foot for bends. Longer hoses may need a gentle slope. A downhill slope is the single most important rule for a gravity hose.
